newsitem.title: USA: New Orleans jury convicts defendants in Espy-related case.
newsitem.headline: New Orleans jury convicts defendants in Espy-related case.

text.p: A New Orleans federal jury on Thursday convicted a prominent attorney and the former head of the nation's second-largest crop insurance company of money laundering in a campaign contribution scheme involving the brother of former Clinton cabinet member Mike Espy, said the office of Independent Counsel Donald Smaltz.

The charges arose out of the ongoing special investigation being conducted of former Agriculture Secretary Espy, who is under criminal investigation for illegally accepting gifts and favors while a member of the cabinet from companies his department was in charge of regulating.

Charles Bakaly of Smaltz' office said New Orleans attorney Alvarez Ferrouillet, campaign manager for Espy's brother Henry, was convicted on 10 counts of money laundering in an attempt to cover up the source of illegal campaign contributions made to help Henry Espy repay almost $200,000 in campaign debts after he unsuccessfully ran for his brother's vacated congressional seat in 1993.
John Hemmingson, former chairman of Crop Growers Corp, one of the largest crop insurance companies in the United States, was also found guilty on three counts of money laundering in the scheme.
Crop Growers was indicted in May for making illegal contributions to Henry Espy in order to gain access to then Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy. The company will go trial in January.
Smaltz has been leading a widespread special investigation of Espy for more than two years.
The probe led to the convictions of the nation's largest fruit cooperative -- Sun-Diamond Growers of California -- for illegally giving gifts and favors to Espy while he served on the cabinet.

The investigation also resulted in criminal indictments and charges being brought against more than a dozen individuals and concerns including the Washington lobbyist for Tyson Foods, the huge Arkansas-based chicken processor whose chairman has long had close ties with President Bill Clinton, a former governor of Arkansas.
